2608.04885.title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Robustness of Vision-Language Models Under Visual and Textual Perturbations
2608.04885.paper_summary: Standard accuracy metrics for VLMs often mask significant reliability failures in sensitive domains. In this work, we utilize a histopathology-validated brain MRI dataset to systematically assess the diagnostic robustness of four VLM families under evidence-preserving perturbations. By reordering anatomical slices and swapping target label positions, we evaluate whether models maintain consistent predictions when clinical evidence remains invariant. Our results reveal significant vulnerabilities in presentation-order stability, with models exhibiting prediction flips in up to 48.9% of cases under simple sequence reversals. We further identify a textual selection bias, where label reordering triggers inconsistent diagnoses in up to 67.8% of cases despite identical visual inputs. Negative-control tests further reveal diagnostic overcommitment: models generate categorical diagnoses in up to 76.1% of cases after expert-annotated lesion slices are removed. These results demonstrate that high accuracy can overestimate clinical reliability, masking sensitivity to sequential presentation and textual framing that is not captured by aggregate accuracy. Our findings highlight the necessity of stability-based metrics for the deployment of VLMs in safety-critical clinical applications. Our evaluation data and code will be made public upon acceptance.
2608.04885.paper_summary_zh: 標準的 VLM 準確性指標往往掩蓋了在敏感領域中的重大可靠性失敗。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們利用經過組織病理學驗證的腦部 MRI 數據集，系統性地評估四個 VLM 家族在保持證據不變的擾動下的診斷穩健性。<lb/>通過重新排序解剖切片和交換目標標籤位置，我們評估模型在臨床證據保持不變的情況下是否能保持一致的預測。<lb/>我們的結果揭示了在呈現順序穩定性方面的重大脆弱性，模型在簡單的序列反轉下顯示出高達 48.9% 的預測翻轉。<lb/>我們進一步識別出一種文本選擇偏見，即標籤重新排序在高達 67.8% 的情況下觸發不一致的診斷，儘管視覺輸入相同。<lb/>負控制測試進一步揭示了診斷過度承諾：在專家註釋的病變切片被移除後，模型在高達 76.1% 的情況下生成類別診斷。<lb/>這些結果表明，高準確率可能高估臨床可靠性，掩蓋了對序列呈現和文本框架的敏感性，而這些並未被整體準確性捕捉到。<lb/>我們的發現強調了在安全關鍵的臨床應用中部署 VLM 所需的基於穩定性的指標。<lb/>我們的評估數據和代碼將在接受後公開。
